content: Chloroquine phosphate is an antimalarial agent. While it has the ability to inhibit certain enzymes, its effects are thought to be partially due to its interaction with DNA. However, the exact mechanism by which chloroquine exerts its plasmodicidal action remains incompletely understood. Chloroquine is effective against the erythrocytic forms of Plasmodium vivax, Plasmodium malariae, and susceptible strains of Plasmodium falciparum. However, it does not act on the gametocytes of P. falciparum or the exoerythrocytic forms of the parasite. In vitro studies using trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica have shown that chloroquine also exhibits amebicidal activity comparable to that of emetine. Resistance to chloroquine is widespread in Plasmodium falciparum, and cases of resistance in Plasmodium vivax have also been reported.
